channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Nonprofit Trees For Houston plants its millionth tree
item.description: Houston Matters visits the celebration and planting of the organization's millionth tree in the region and talks with executive director, Barry Ward.

item.title: Runoffs, Rifts, and the Fight for Texas Power
item.description: Co-hosts Brandon Rottinghaus and Jeronimo Cortina delve into the latest news in politics

item.title: Texas AG opens probe into Houston anti-fascist group accused of ‘doxing’ neo-Nazis
item.description: Ken Paxton's office announced Friday it has issued a request for records and documents from the Screwston Anti-Fascist Committee to identify the scope of their alleged legal violations, including an alleged connection to the Prairieland ICE Detention Center shooting.

item.title: Waller ISD elementary school evacuated, two students taken to hospital over gas odor
item.description: Harris County emergency services ventilated Roberts Road Elementary and said Friday afternoon the situation was under control.

item.title: Hello Houston (February 6, 2026)
item.description: Today: We listen to the latest Cold Coffee featuring Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo, author Jeffrey Sonnenfeld discusses his upcoming book, and Ernie Manouse broadcasts live from the Houston Home and Garden Show.

item.title: Parents of missing camper sue Camp Mystic after deadly Texas Hill Country flood
item.description: The lawsuit, the fifth against the camp, alleges that failures by camp leadership led to the death of 8-year-old Cecilia Steward, who remains missing more than seven months after the flood.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (February 6, 2026)
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters – we have “The Commuter Cut” – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: Democrats, Harris County residents sue to stop ICE operations in the Houston area
item.description: The lawsuit, filed in federal court on Friday, asks for a decisive legal opinion affirming citizens do not need to carry proof of citizenship on them at all times.

item.title: Professors, students push back as Texas A&M regents increase curriculum oversight
item.description: The American Association of University Professors has started a petition against policies that limit classroom discussions about topics including race and gender.

item.title: University of Houston asks professors to sign agreement ‘not to indoctrinate’ students
item.description: The new memo has given pause to some UH professors as the university seeks to comply with state legislation overhauling higher education, which has garnered national scrutiny.
